horizon_driver: Japan: frequent PM turnover within a 4yr Diet term; Korea: single non-renewable 5-year presidential term (Lee admin since June 2025) — both shorter than the multi-decade demographic and alliance structures that actually bind them

constraints.source: US-Japan Security Treaty / US-ROK Mutual Defense Treaty, decades of interoperability and nuclear-umbrella dependence
constraints.breaks_under: not observed to break; both states have instead increased defense spending and alliance coordination since 2022

constraints.source: Samsung/SK Hynix China-based fab revenue dependence
constraints.breaks_under: already bending: Korea's chip exports to China surged 243% YoY in May 2026 on AI-driven memory demand even as the two firms operate China fabs under US-granted (and in Sept 2025, briefly revoked) annual license exemptions

constraints.source: decades of sub-replacement fertility in both countries; policy responses (childcare subsidies, immigration liberalization) have not reversed the trend
constraints.breaks_under: does not break; treat as structural physics, not a strategic choice

stated_vs_revealed.stated: South Korea is aligned with the US-led effort to contain Chinese access to advanced chip technology.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Korea's chip exports to China surged 243% YoY in May 2026, driven by Beijing's AI push and DRAM shortages, and Samsung/SK Hynix continue operating China-based memory fabs under annual US license exemptions (revoked briefly Sept 2025, restored in 2026) — commercial memory-chip demand from China is currently overriding the containment posture wherever license terms allow it.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Alignment is compliance-bounded, not preference-based: Korea follows the letter of US export licensing while maximizing whatever commercial space remains within it.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Japan is pursuing 'China+1' supply-chain derisking as a strategic choice to reduce vulnerability.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Japan's export share and competitiveness versus China have simply eroded on commercial grounds: South Korea and Taiwan each surpassed Japan in total exports for the first time in H1 2026, and Japan's exports to China declined post-RCEP while Korea's grew — this looks more like competitive displacement than deliberate strategic derisking.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The 'derisking' narrative partly launders a loss of competitiveness that has separate commercial causes (memory/AI-chip specialization gap versus Korea and Taiwan).

stated_vs_revealed.stated: South Korea's Lee administration (since June 2025) is normalizing relations with China without weakening the US alliance.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Seoul is pursuing exactly that dual-track: improved China relations (post-THAAD thaw) run concurrently with an unchanged US alliance structure and unchanged THAAD deployment — a genuine both-sides hedge rather than a realignment in either direction.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Small but real: this is the beginning of a divergence from Japan, which has been more assertively aligned with US tool-export controls (ASML/Tokyo Electron-adjacent policy) — the Cartographer's flagged split condition on China exposure is starting to show even absent a Taiwan-conflict spike.

tripwires.if: US-China Taiwan-conflict risk indicators rise materially (e.g. a sustained PLA quarantine/blockade exercise)
tripwires.then: Japan tightens tool and materials export controls faster and more visibly than Korea within roughly one quarter, producing an observable policy divergence — this is the trigger condition for splitting the merged actor

tripwires.if: the US revokes Samsung/SK Hynix China-fab license exemptions again without renewal (as briefly occurred Sept 2025)
tripwires.then: Korea faces an acute forced choice between US alliance compliance and China revenue, testing the hedge in a way Japan (with less China-fab exposure) does not face equally

tripwires.if: the Bank of Japan continues rate normalization and triggers a yen-carry-trade unwind
tripwires.then: both Japan and Korea face capital-repatriation shocks given their creditor-nation asset bases (Japan recently slipped to the world's #3 net creditor behind Germany and China as of 2025 data)

what_would_change_my_mind: A clean, sustained divergence in formal export-control policy between Tokyo and Seoul (not just commercial outcomes) over 2+ quarters would justify actually splitting this into ST_JP and ST_KR. Current evidence shows commercial/trade divergence (Korea's China chip surplus vs Japan's export erosion) but not yet a clear policy-level split — recommend keeping merged but flagging the China-exposure gap as an explicit watch item rather than the Taiwan-conflict-only trigger the Cartographer specified.
